item.text: A star’s apparent brightness depends on both its intrinsic luminosity and its distance from us. Light spreads out as it travels, so a very luminous star far away can look as bright as a faint star nearby. Dust between us and a star can also dim its light. Thus, stars with equal apparent brightness may differ enormously in true energy output, size, temperature, and evolutionary stage.
